trade_history.catalyst: Unexpected inventory builds or weak refinery demand pressuring prices.

Crude prices are tumbling amid easing Strait of Hormuz supply concerns, rising regional exports, and G-7 plans for strategic crude and diesel releases. Despite lingering tail-risk commentary regarding tanker vulnerabilities, physical supply normalization and prevailing bearish momentum dominate the near-term outlook.

Escalating maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz threaten vital crude export flows, outweighing short-term recovery reports and reinforcing a strong geopolitical risk premium. This supply vulnerability, compounded by EIA reports of inventory depletion from the Iran conflict, drives aggressive bullish momentum that easily overrides minor technical resistance.
